overview: January 1942 despatch with Mexican clippings on a rumored Japanese submarine off Mazatlán and the Navy's denial.

people.name: Raleigh A. Gibson
people.role: First Secretary of Embassy, U.S. Embassy in Mexico

subfiles.about: Despatch from the U.S. Embassy in Mexico City transmitting newspaper articles on rumors and investigations regarding an alleged Japanese submarine off Mazatlán.
subfiles.summary: Gibson sends clippings on fishermen's report of a submarine off Mazatlán and the Mexican Navy's denial.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Gibson transmitting news reports on alleged Japanese submarine near Mazatlán

subfiles.about: Newspaper clipping detailing claims by three local fishermen that they observed an unidentified submarine signalling near Mazatlán.
subfiles.summary: Excélsior reports fishermen saw lights off Mazatlán, possibly a submarine.
subfiles.title: Clipping from Excélsior: 'Presúmese que un submarino navega en las aguas inmediatas a Mazatlán'

subfiles.about: Newspaper clipping reporting the Mexican Ministry of the Navy's categorical denial of Japanese submarine sightings off Baja California and Sinaloa.
subfiles.summary: El Nacional reports Mexico's Navy denied any Japanese submarine sightings.
subfiles.title: Clipping from El Nacional: 'Ningún submarino del Japón ha sido visto en nuestro litoral'
